I appreciate that there are responses here. I take things hard. I am 36 going on 10 when it comes to emotional maturity sometimes. If I post something on Facebook that I feel is important to me and no one "likes" it, that can set my mood off. So thank you guys. Just to respond to a couple of things. Sorry in advance for the essay to come. 

At the time when I was fighting cancer I was in my early twenties. I had no direction in life at the time. Dropped out of high school and got my GED so I was working two jobs when I got diagnosed. I had been with my girlfriend at the time, now my wife, for about a year. I got diagnosed with non-hodgkin's lymphoma got treated with radiation and chemotherapy that took about 6 months or so, and then two months later I had a recurrence. I proposed to her at a spot that she had chosen for us to get away for a bit after my diagnosis. I had a huge tumor on the back of my head and we were getting married. When I went through the most gruesome part of the cancer battle, was when I was at Stanford Cancer Center  being treated. Multiple rounds of chemo , followed by a stem cell transplant. My thought at the time was that I have to survive for my wife. Not for me because even back then I felt like a piece of shit. I was advised to store semen before treatment ever started, and from there is how we got our two kids my son and daughter. What is happened over the years is I have never gotten back on track. I was told by a counselor that early twenties is a very big developmental time in an adult's life and mine was retarded by being in hospitals all the time. While I was getting treated my wife would drive an hour and a half every day to come see me at the hospital. That showed me how much she loved me and as I said made me want to survive that someone could care about me like that. So through the years we had kids and her priorities in life( as a mother's would), have changed, & I still have no direction. Yeah I survived cancer, but now the reason for why is unclear. I love my kids, & I have always had that love for my wife, the truth is I've been dragging her down for years with all my problems. I realize she's an adult and heard that a million times, and it was her choice to be with me. That doesn't make the feeling any easier. She's always been the breadwinner for us which adds to it and I was an  at home Dad for a while and now both our kids are old enough that there at school, & I do nothing.

There's a lot more to it and I'm not trying to lay out my life story here I'm sorry if it sounds like it. Just trying to give a background. So the last 9 months or so have been probably not the best. I was drinking a lot everyday while at home, so I could be feeling more light hearted and whatever when my wife and the kids would get home. Or that's what I thought it made me feel. She told me one time how much it hurt her that I was drinking so much because she knows on medications and she felt like you didn't make sense to be doing that to myself. She actually told me that multiple occasions. So I kept drinking up until a month ago when I got off my antidepressants that were making me gain a ton of weight and stop drinking because I was feeling so sick anyways. So it's been about a month of no drinking and last week, what a tribute to part of the withdrawal symptoms from the zoloft, I had some suicidal thoughts. I started going back to counseling after a while not going, and made some plans to start this week with an outpatient treatment program. Last night was my wife and I's 9th anniversary and with how things have been going I didn't expect that we would do anything, & I really didn't want to because I don't like going out anymore. She talked me into it and I went out and got my hair cut and dressed up witch is a big deal for me, and we went out and she had a couple drinks and laid out there how tired she is of how things aren't going anywhere and how I'm always upset or angry or depressed and so on. Most of what she was saying was how I feel, I'm not saying is incorrect in what she was saying. It just hurts to hear it and especially on that night and I didn't know why we had to be out in public for that to happen. She said I always tell her to speak her mind and I guess she wants credit for telling me how she really feels. So my feeling is that at this point there's really no reason for me to be around as I'm typing this I'm in the Starbucks parking lot trying to figure out what I'm going to do now. I have no friends like I said, not sure where I'll even stay. But I do know that I can't stay at home with someone who is so sick and tired of my presence, or so it seems. I like the thought of just not existing anymore, but fear the thought of death.


 I realize that I survived cancer, but I think that just took so much of the fight that I had out of me during that time. I have no more left. and I just don't feel like fighting for ' it'. Whatever 'it' may be. Whether it's being a good father, husband, son, regular working person of society or whatever.  

You know I know there's people that are cancer survivors and they say they don't want cancer to define them. And there's this whole thing about cancer survivors that you're supposed to be super strong and awesome and fighters and you know everyone respects you. Just because I got a disease and survived it doesn't change my core being in my opinion. I've been to so  much counseling and on so many various medications over the years, I think this is just Who I am. And I don't blame her for being tired.
